layout_notes: person stands in the left third of the frame; snowball flight arcs from the hand up through the middle of the frame to the far upper right corner; ground line runs along the bottom of the whole frame

parts.name: thrower_head
parts.notes: same size on every key; leans back on windup, forward on release

parts.name: thrower_torso
parts.notes: leans back when cocked, arcs forward on release

parts.name: thrower_back_leg
parts.notes: pushes off, heel lifts on follow-through

parts.name: thrower_throwing_arm
parts.how: two-segment line shoulder to elbow to wrist
parts.notes: cocked back behind head, snaps forward past ear, ends low in front

parts.name: thrower_off_arm
parts.how: two-segment line shoulder to elbow to hand
parts.notes: reaches forward for balance, swings down on follow-through

parts.name: snowball
parts.notes: in the fist at start, just off the fingers at release, far up-right at end

parts.name: ground
parts.notes: one shared ground line, identical points on every key

keys.name: start
keys.notes: weight on back leg, throwing arm bent up behind the head, snowball held at the fist, torso leaning back

keys.name: release
keys.notes: arm fully extended forward and up, wrist at release point, snowball a finger-width ahead of the hand, front leg planted, torso lunged forward

keys.name: end
keys.notes: throwing arm swept down and across the body, torso bent forward, snowball high in the far upper right of the frame

gaps.notes: short wind-up travel of the arm and body, fewer inbetweens
snowball travels the farthest distance across the frame while the body settles into follow-through; same ease as the first half so speed does not flip
